newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West spot power weakens ahead of warm weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West spot power weakens ahead of warm weather.

text.p: Spot power prices in the U.S. West dipped Friday amid above-normal temperatures in both the Northwest and Southwest, market sources said.
"The forecast is for record highs in the Northwest this weekend--high 50s to low 60s (Fahrenheit)," said one trader.
The Bonneville Power Administration's decision to expand offers and cut prices for Sunday through Tuesday schedulings also put downward pressure on the Northwest market, sources said.
In Southern California, the re-emergence of hot, dry Santa Ana winds has pushed daytime temperatures into the 80s.
Traders also said weaker San Juan cash natural gas prices and the long holiday weekend contributed to the western power market's bearish tone.
They noted that coming power plant maintenance outages were not having much impact.

In Colorado, a 428 megawatt (MW) coal-fired unit at the Craig station was set to shut Friday night and expected to restart Monday morning. A 720-MW unit at the Navajo coal-fired power plant in Arizona was scheduled to shut Saturday until December 18 for maintenance.
Monday prices for California-Oregon border (COB) firm, on-peak power were quoted $23.00-24.00, down from $24.00-25.00 for Friday deals.
Off-peak COB quotes were lower at $17.50-18.00.
Mid-Columbia prices for Monday firm, on-peak power were quoted $19.00-20.00, down from $20.00-21.00.
In the Southwest, Palo Verde firm on-peak power for Monday was quoted $21.00-22.00, down slightly from $21.00-23.00.
Next-day Four Corners was also slightly weaker at $21.50-23.00.
Cash Palo Verde for December was quoted $21.50-22.25, down from $21.70-21.80. COB for December was quoted $22.75-23.25, down from $22.90-23.25.
